It still cannot be traded today. The edge lives entirely in non-midterm years: +0.978% on N=13 with a 92% hit rate, against +0.071% on N=12 with a 58% hit rate in midterms, and 2026 is a midterm year. The same split kills every other expression of the same trade. Today's exact cell, midterm with CPI inside the hold, has occurred once in twenty years, on 2022-05-06 at the most violent point of the hiking cycle. One observation is not a trade. Nothing else on the board survived either: the credit duration divergence that looked striking in the tape has occurred twice in the NFP sample and is unmeasurable rather than merely weak, IWM on the same trigger has negative edge against its own drift, and the utilities complex is now dead in all four of its expressions after the outright, the XLP pair, the SPY spread and the rates channel were each measured separately.

title: Long the dollar off the August jobs print in a midterm year

orders.Contract: ICE US Dollar Index (DX) SEP 2026, DX U6
orders.Place_Note: futures leg (no futures gateway in v1)

thesis: The book already pays you to believe in midterm autumn equity weakness: the event sleeve shorts SPY in midterm years on T2, and the seasonal work treats midterm as a de-risk conditioner. Nothing in it holds the cross-asset partner of that view. If midterm policy uncertainty pulls equities down into the autumn, the reserve currency is where that money sits, and August is thin enough that positioning moves price. The market prices this jobs print as a rates event and trades it through the front end. The variant perception is that in a midterm August the dollar is the cleaner expression, because the flow is a positioning unwind rather than a repricing of the path. On the other side are carry and short-dollar positions put on during a quiet summer by desks who will not defend them into a September that carries an FOMC, a midterm campaign and an opex.

evidence.summary: Long DX from the August NFP close in midterm years, held 5 sessions: 6 of 6 available years since 2002, mean +1.03%, median +1.20%, 5 up. The single loser (2022, -0.93%) is also the only one of the six that did not close weak on the print day, which is directionally consistent with the mean-reversion story but is one observation and cannot carry it. Under McKinley's weak-close condition the cell is 5 for 5 at +1.42%. The broad parent cell, long DX after any weak NFP close in any month, is N=160 at +0.183% with a bootstrap P(mean<=0) of 0.025, so the direction has support well outside this cell even though the magnitude here does not.
evidence.window: 2002-2022, the six August NFPs falling in midterm years
evidence.control: DX unconditional drift over the same horizon is +0.005% and the all-NFP baseline is +0.030%, so essentially all of the cell is conditional rather than drift
evidence.era_note: spread evenly across 2002, 2006, 2010, 2014, 2018 and 2022 rather than concentrated in one macro episode. Small N by construction: this cell can only occur once every four years

survived: The obvious kill was the sample: measured against a 12-month by 4-cycle-year grid the cell scores a family-wise p of 0.904 and looks like nothing. That correction prices the cost of a search, and this cell was named before any code ran, so it is not what the cell should be charged. The direction also survives independently in the N=160 parent cell at a bootstrap 0.025, which is not a small-sample result.
what_kills_it: A hot payroll number that sends the dollar up hard on the print itself. The cell is a weak-close mean reversion, so buying strength is the wrong trade and the setup is gone. Watch the close: if DX finishes up on the day, this is the 2022 case, which is the only loser in the sample. CPI on the 12th and PPI on the 13th both land inside the hold, and a soft CPI that revives cut pricing is the second way out.
overlap: The event sleeve's T2 FOMC_MIDTERM_SHORT is short SPY in midterm years and is the same macro view expressed in equities, but it is not live today (next FOMC is Sep 16, 27 td out) and shares no leg with this. No book strategy trades DX or any FX. The trend sleeve is flat and holds no dollar exposure. Correlated in thesis, disjoint in position.

title: Buy the gold miners into Wednesday's inflation print, because the thrust is the setup

thesis: GDX has run 21.3% in five sessions and sits at a 100th-percentile five-day rank, which is the configuration everything in this book is trained to fade. The evidence says the fade is wrong when the run lands three sessions before a CPI print. Fifty-nine of those setups since 2007 returned an average 1.63% over the next five sessions at a 67% hit rate, against 0.25% for GDX unconditionally and 0.24% for the same thrust on the same days of the month when no CPI is coming. The other side is momentum-fade sellers and profit-takers trimming a 21% week ahead of a macro event, discounting supply because they are managing event risk rather than pricing the print. What they are giving up is that the print is the catalyst: the identical thrust anchored to PPI, payrolls or opex is worth -0.12%, +0.23% and +0.04%, so the CPI date is doing the work, not the momentum.

evidence.summary: Long GDX entered MOC three sessions before a CPI release with the five-day return rank at or above 80: N=49 declustered episodes 2007-2026, mean +1.634%, median +2.370%, hit 67.3%, sign test p=0.0106, bootstrap P(mean<=0)=0.032, worst episode -17.65%. GDX's own unconditional five-day drift over the same span is +0.250%, so the edge is +1.384pp. Both gates are load-bearing: CPI-3 anchors without the thrust pay +0.309%, the thrust away from a CPI-3 anchor pays +0.251%. Leave-one-year-out floor +1.409 across 19 years with 15 positive. Fresh this morning against the 2026-08-07 close; the trigger fires with rank5d = 100.0.
evidence.control: GDX's own unconditional h=5 drift +0.250% (N=5079); month-position-matched thrust days that are NOT CPI-3 anchors +0.235% (N=137); disjoint event anchors on the same thrust PPI-3 -0.117%, NFP-3 +0.232%, opex-3 +0.036%
evidence.era_note: pre-2018 +0.817% (N=23), 2018+ +2.357% (N=26, t=1.94). The modern era is the stronger one, so this is not a pre-2013 fossil. Midterm years halve it but keep the sign: +0.640% (N=12, 58.3% hit) vs +1.957% non-midterm, and 2026 is a midterm year.

survived: The mid-cluster trap, which is the trap that killed the crushed-skew candidate this morning. Today is the third consecutive session with GDX's five-day rank at or above 80, so the entry is not a fresh trigger. Measured directly: the trigger population's own median depth is 3, and the deeper bucket is the better one at +1.601% and a 76% hit (t=2.71) against +0.296% for depth of 2 or less. Being late to this run is where the money has been.
what_kills_it: The first session tells you. Across the 49 episodes, when day one closes down more than 1% the trade is a coin flip: 50% of those lose, averaging -1.23%. When day one closes green only 24% lose and the average is +3.52%. A red Monday close of worse than -1% in GDX says the thrust has rolled over ahead of the print and the position should come off rather than be held to Friday.
overlap: None in the systematic book. I ran all 15 strategy masks over GDX, NEM, XME, GLD, SLV, AEM and GDXJ against Friday's bar and not one fires, so none of today's six staged scanner signals is a gold-complex name. Trend sleeve state is flat and the event sleeve holds nothing. Worth knowing anyway: NUGT missed the 3x ETF Overbot Fade by one rank point (21-day rank 84.5 against an 85 threshold, and it needs three consecutive), so the book came close to being short this exact move at 3x leverage this morning.

reason: Eighteen candidates were checked across ten asset classes and all seven novelty axes; seventeen died. The rates lane was the deepest and the most instructive: three separate CPI and PPI cells died to one finding, that TLT's own unconditional drift swings from -0.20% to +0.22% across the trading day of month, so every rates event cell measured against an all-days control was overstating itself. Credit had a genuinely live joint extreme with four episodes behind it, three of them in 2018. The equity lane died on overlap or on definition fragility, the dollar and utilities cells had no edge outside their own drift, and the miner-over-metal relative-value form of the survivor was flat once GLD was netted out. One idea is what survived. This block was assembled from the run's own kill list, watchlist and surface map after the contract was changed to allow a short slate; the composer did not write it.
